PortalLSHTM online application, then the scholarships portal link emailed after you apply ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Two steps. First, apply for a London-based MSc and pay the non-refundable £50 admissions fee. Second, LSHTM emails a link to its scholarship portal where you select 'LSHTM Fund Scholarship'. No separate scholarship fee is stated. Both steps must be done by the scholarship deadline. The 2027-28 page is not published yet; the link is the 2026-27 page.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against LSHTM's 2026-27 Fund Scholarship page and 'How to apply' pages; the 2027-28 deadline was not found.

01

What it pays

  • Full overseas-rate tuition, including mandatory field trip fees, plus a tax-free stipend of £22,000.
  • You pay a £50 admissions fee. No separate scholarship fee is stated.

02

Who can apply

  • Nationals of, and resident in, World Bank low- and middle-income countries. Bangladesh is a World Bank lower-middle-income country, so you should qualify; confirm the exact wording on the 2027-28 page.
  • A first or upper-second-class degree (or equivalent), and an offer for a London-based intensive MSc. Joint programmes (Global Mental Health, Health Policy Planning and Financing, One Health, Veterinary Epidemiology) are excluded.

03

Dates that matter

  • The 2027-28 deadline is not published. LSHTM adds 2027-28 adverts as funding becomes available.
  • For reference only, the 2026-27 deadline was 16:00 GMT, Wednesday 4 March 2026, with both steps done by then.
  • LSHTM's general MSc closing date for 2027-28 entry is 25 Jul 2027.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A funded MSc Epidemiology at LSHTM gives research training, publications and a UK network. It does not give a UK licence and does not help the US Match timeline. A 2027 start collides with the internship, so the 2028-29 round is the realistic one.

    A single scholarship across all LSHTM master's applicants.

  2. 02

    The scholarship form only appears after you submit the MSc application.

    Plan from last year's early-March deadline but wait for the 2027-28 page.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: timeline

    Starting in 2027 overlaps the internship and delays the Match.

06

The honest recommendation

Treat it as a lottery ticket for the 2028-29 round. Keep your application documents ready, watch the LSHTM scholarships page, and do not plan finances around it.

Before you board

PortalDAAD Portal (link appears only while a call is running) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Register on the DAAD Portal and upload documents under 'Attachments'. DAAD states no charge for applying. You must also win admission to a German master's yourself, and DAAD does not pay tuition at the host university.

How this was checked: DAAD scholarship database entry for the Master's Study Scholarship (Application Procedure and Submitting an Application tabs), 3 Nov 2026; the fee is listed as NOT FOUND, but no charge is mentioned anywhere on the page.

01

What it pays

  • EUR 992 a month, plus health, accident and liability insurance.
  • A EUR 460 yearly study allowance and a travel allowance.
  • DAAD does not cover tuition; check the host university's own fees.
  • Funding runs 10 to 24 months, only with admission to the named host university.

02

Who can apply

  • Graduates with a first degree finished by the start of funding and, as a rule, no more than 6 years old at the deadline.
  • No professional-experience requirement is listed on the programme page (EPOS, by contrast, needs at least 2 years).
  • You must arrange your own admission to a full-time master's at a German university.
  • You cannot apply if you have lived in Germany more than 15 months at the deadline.

03

Dates that matter

  • 1 Jun to 31 Aug 2026: Bangladesh window, now closed (selection Feb 2027, funding from Oct 2027).
  • DAAD updates deadlines every spring and they are country-specific, so re-check the programme page.
  • The next call is not published; if the usual yearly pattern holds it would be for funding from October 2028 (not confirmed).

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

For Europe this is the best-fitting funded master's you have: two years in Germany to reach B2 and C1 medical German, then Approbation. A funded start from October 2028 would also come after your internship, which a 2027 start would not.

For the US, a master's adds research and letters but takes 1 to 2 years. It does not replace Step 1, a paid research job or Step 2 CK, so Match 2029 would move to about 2030.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: it has closed

    There is no way into the 2027 round now.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: two applications

    You need German admission and a DAAD award; neither guarantees the other.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: a master's is not a licence

    Approbation is a separate process with its own exams.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: the 6-year rule

    It runs from your degree, so delay beyond about 2032 costs eligibility.

06

The honest recommendation

Do not chase this cycle. Use 2027 to pick two or three German master's, get a research output, and be ready to apply the moment the next Bangladesh window opens.

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: your region's right-to-study agency (example ER.GO, Emilia-Romagna) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

DSU is claimed online from the regional agency for the region where your university sits, under that agency's yearly call. Non-EU students also complete pre-enrolment on Universitaly for admission and visa. The family papers (ISEE parificato, legalised and translated) cost money to prepare, but no fee for the claim itself is mentioned.

How this was checked: ER.GO guide to the 2026/27 call, UNIMORE and University of Parma fee pages, 3 Nov 2026; no fee found and the 2027/28 deadlines are NOT FOUND (regional calls appear in summer 2027).

01

What it pays

  • About EUR 7,171 or more a year in cash, per the board card.
  • Full or partial university fee exemption, canteen access and accommodation (as the region provides).
  • It is paid by the region, so it varies by agency (ER.GO, DiSCo, EDISU and others).

02

Who can apply

  • Students enrolled or pre-enrolled at a public Italian university.
  • Family income and assets under the regional ceilings; the board card lists ISEE up to EUR 28,339.88 and ISPE up to EUR 61,608.48 for 2026/27.
  • As a Bangladeshi you need an ISEE parificato, with income and asset documents legalised and translated.
  • Later years need a minimum number of credits.

03

Dates that matter

  • Regional calls for 2027/28 appear in summer 2027 (ER.GO publishes around July).
  • Benefit deadlines usually fall in late summer or autumn.
  • Italian university admission and Universitaly pre-enrolment come first.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

It can make an Italian master's close to free, which protects your USD 30,000 for exams and US rotations. But the degree takes about two years and would push Match from 2029 to roughly 2030 or later.

It does not license you in Italy. Recognition of your MBBS and Italian language are separate steps.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: not a competition

    It is a means-tested claim, not a prize; you may apply while pre-enrolled, but you need an Italian university place to use it.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: paperwork

    Legalising and translating Bangladeshi family papers takes months, so start early.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: credits

    Keeping the money needs study progress, which competes with USMLE preparation.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: region matters

    The portal, call and deadline depend on the region of your chosen university.

06

The honest recommendation

Treat DSU as a cost-saver for an Italian master's you already want, not a reason to go to Italy. Choose the course first, then check that region's call.

UK Wellcome and MRC doctoral programmes are not applied for centrally. Wellcome says to contact the programme directly, and UKRI/MRC studentships are run by universities and partnerships. UKRI normally caps international appointees at about 30% and funds only the Home fee, so the overseas fee gap is often not covered.

Before you board

Portaluni-assist: Pay & submit (many German universities); others apply direct ↗ (opens in a new tab)

On the uni-assist route the fee is EUR 75 for the first course and EUR 30 for each additional course, per application semester, and it is charged again if you reapply. Some uni-assist universities cover the fee. Universities that take direct applications set their own arrangements and many charge nothing. Semester contributions, a blocked account and living costs are separate.

How this was checked: Checked uni-assist's Pay & submit and handling-fees page on 3 Nov 2026; no single national deadline or direct-route fee exists, so those are NOT FOUND.

01

What it costs

  • Tuition is usually nil at public universities, but not everywhere: Baden-Wurttemberg charges non-EU students tuition, per the verified notes.
  • You still pay semester contributions, living costs and a blocked account for the visa. The board estimates about USD 16-18k in year 1 and about USD 30k over two years.
  • uni-assist fee: EUR 75 plus EUR 30 per extra course.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone with a recognised degree that meets the programme's own entry rules. Check each programme page for the public health or statistics background it asks for.
  • Whether a given programme uses uni-assist, the VPD pre-check or its own portal must be read on that programme's page.
  • English-taught programmes need English proof; check each programme's language rules.

03

Dates that matter

  • No national deadline. Typical German master's windows are around 15 January for summer starts and 15 July for winter starts, but each programme sets its own.
  • uni-assist says document checks take weeks, so apply early.
  • A winter 2027 start would overlap your internship; the board's date is about 15 Jan 2028 for a summer 2028 start.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

This is your one fully realistic way to a European degree on a USD 30,000 budget, but it spends most of that budget. A two-year degree starting 2027 or 2028 would also take you away from the 2029 Match timetable and give no US clinical experience.

A master's is not a medical licence; German medical licensing is a separate process that the verified notes do not cover.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: Budget

    Two years of living costs take about your whole USD 30k, leaving little for USMLE fees, electives and ERAS.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: Match timing

    A degree running to 2029 or 2030 makes your graduation year older and gives no US clinical experience.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: Not a licence

    A master's is not a medical licence; licensing is a separate process.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: Deadlines vary

    There is no single date, so every programme must be checked on its own page.

06

The honest recommendation

Keep it as a funded-by-yourself Plan B for Europe. Short-list two or three English-taught programmes now, price them, and decide after you see your Step 1 plan. Do not commit the USD 30k until the US route is clearer.

Before you board

PortalUniversity of Manchester application portal (link on the programme page) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

No application fee is stated on the programme page or the pages read, so check inside the portal before assuming it is free. In the portal choose Postgraduate Research, entry year 2027/28, intake September (the studentship itself begins October 2027), funding Research Council / MRC PhD Studentship / Awarded / Fully Funded, and name the main supervisor only. Each of your up to two projects is a separate application.

How this was checked: University of Manchester MRC NW-DMS programme page and the Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health PhD pages, 9 Nov 2026; application fee NOT FOUND.

01

What it pays

  • Tuition is funded at the home or international rate, so the usual overseas-fee gap on UK studentships is covered here.
  • A stipend at the UKRI rate for four years. The UKRI minimum is £21,805 from 1 Oct 2026 (£20,780 before). The Manchester page prints no figure and the 2027/28 rate may be higher.
  • Your $30,000 budget stays free for USMLE fees and US experience.
  • Application fee: not confirmed on the official page. Check the portal.

02

Who can apply

  • UK and international applicants.
  • A First or Upper Second-class UK honours degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant discipline. No master's is required, though many successful applicants have one or research experience.
  • Whether an MBBS counts is not stated. Ask fbmh.doctoralacademy.admissions@manchester.ac.uk, in the same email as your English-waiver question.
  • You can apply for up to two projects, each a separate application with a supporting statement tailored to that project.

03

Dates that matter

  • Projects and applications opened 30 Oct 2026.
  • Deadline: Fri 27 Nov 2026 (no closing time stated). Plan to submit by about 25 Nov.
  • Interviews w/c 8 Feb 2027 on Teams, only for applicants a supervisor has nominated, with a presentation of up to 10 minutes. Others are told they were unsuccessful.
  • Studentships awarded w/c 22 Feb 2027; studentship begins October 2027.

04

What the file needs

  • A supporting statement tailored to the project: no word limit, 2 to 4 pages recommended. No separate research statement.
  • A CV, degree certificates and final or interim transcripts, and official English certificates if applicable.
  • Two referees who know your academic ability; one can be clinical or work-based. Their emails must be institutional, not personal. Referees get an automatic request on submission, and you cannot be nominated without references.
  • No English test at application. It is a condition of any offer: typically IELTS 6.5 overall (5.5 each part, 6.0 writing) or TOEFL iBT 90, and some programmes ask 7.0. Tests are valid for 2 years.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A funded UK PhD gives you a real research record and a supervisor's letter, and projects in modelling, vaccination or prescribing data suit an MBBS with manuscripts. It also takes four years from October 2027, so it replaces the Step 1, paid US research job and Step 2 CK plan rather than adding to it, and the Match slips well past 2029.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: supervisor first

    The programme calls contacting the supervisor one of the most important steps, and only nominated applicants are interviewed. Emails need to go out this week.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: MBBS equivalence

    The page does not say an MBBS counts as the qualifying degree, and competition is described as very high.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: lab-heavy list

    Most advertised projects are lab-based. Your file is strongest on population, clinical-data or modelling projects; pick the project before writing the statement.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: start date

    October 2027 begins before your internship is likely to end in late 2027.

07

The honest recommendation

A long shot with a real chance only if a supervisor backs you. If a population-health project fits and a supervisor replies, apply by about 25 Nov to one or two projects. If nobody replies by about 19 Nov, drop it and keep your energy on the 1 Dec US files and Step 1.

Four grants a year, nomination-only: apply to the Master's by 1 Dec

The Eric Bleumink Fellowship pays a Groningen Master's in full for four students a year, but you cannot apply for it. The only action is a complete Master's application before 1 Dec 2026; the Admissions Office picks nominees in the first week of January.

✦ Drafted from your uploaded notes, then checked against the official pages on 9 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

  • Poor fitUS Match, 2029 planA Master's in Groningen does not feed a US Match, and the fellowship requires you to return home.
  • MixedPractising in EuropeA Dutch research master is a real European credential but does not license you to practise.
  • Good fitYour interestsThe MSc Interdisciplinary Research in Health Dynamics is the one true epidemiology and population-health programme at Groningen.

Before you board

PortalNo fellowship application: apply to the Master's (fellowship page) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

The fellowship has no application. The EUR 100 is the non-refundable Groningen application fee for applicants with a non-Dutch diploma, paid once per academic year, and the Admissions Office cannot review your file until it is received. Complete the Master's application before 1 Dec 2026 so an admission offer exists before February. Do not contact the fellowship with an application: suitable candidates are told of a nomination.

How this was checked: University of Groningen fellowship page, the Eric Bleumink Fellowship Rules and Regulations PDF (updated Nov 2024) and the non-Dutch-qualification fee page, 9 Nov 2026.

01

What it pays

  • Tuition fees paid in full.
  • EUR 1,250 a month living allowance, a EUR 275 settling allowance and EUR 310 a year for books and study material.
  • Return flights between Amsterdam and the airport nearest your home (economy, excess baggage not covered), a train from Schiphol to Groningen, and insurance through AON. No clothing allowance.
  • Without it, the MSc IRHD costs EUR 24,900 a year for non-EU students in 2027-28.

02

Who can apply

  • Master's only (1 or 2 years), September start only, any field. You cannot apply for the fellowship itself.
  • Bangladesh is on the country list, in the first-preference Least Developed Countries tier on the likely reading of the table. No Bangladeshi university is on the partner list, so that preference does not apply.
  • Excellent bachelor's results, English proficiency, no other means of financing and no simultaneous other Groningen scholarship.
  • IRHD names Medicine among admissible bachelor's degrees, but a foreign MBBS is not named. Ask irhd@umcg.nl (address not verified).

03

Dates that matter

  • Before 1 Dec 2026: complete the Master's application, including the EUR 100 fee.
  • First week of January 2027: the Admissions Office selects nominees. Nominees send a motivation letter within one week.
  • Files go to the committee before 1 Feb; fellows are informed before 1 March. The web page says nominees hear before 1 Feb, so no contact by then means you were not nominated.
  • The IRHD programme page lists 1 May 2027 as its deadline, but the Groningen International Guide lists 1 March for non-EU; the 1 Dec target governs the Bleumink route anyway.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

The IRHD research master teaches epidemiology and statistics, and entry includes a statistics exam and an interview. It is a European credential, not a licensing step, and the fellowship's return-home commitment sits awkwardly with a US Match plan.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: four grants

    Hundreds apply and four awards are made. You cannot apply; you are nominated or not.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: the return-home statement

    Fellows may not take paid work in the Netherlands, there is no family provision, and they state they will return to their own country at the end.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: you must be admitted first

    An admission offer must exist before February, and without the fellowship tuition is EUR 24,900 a year, far above a $30,000 budget over a year or two.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: IRHD selection

    A statistics entrance exam, then an interview with a short presentation on a past research project and your motivation, with results in 2 to 3 weeks.

06

The honest recommendation

Only apply to IRHD if you would genuinely take a Master's there and could afford the fees without the fellowship. The fellowship is an upside, not a plan. Ask irhd@umcg.nl about your MBBS and the exam before paying the fee.

✓

PortalRadboud OSIRIS Application (admission and scholarship) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Apply for an English-taught master's and request the scholarship in OSIRIS. Submit by 31 Jan 2027 23:59 CET and complete by 14 Feb 2027 23:59 CET, with two reference letters and a CV. An application fee was not confirmed on the page checked. The NL Scholarship page is ru.nl/en/education/scholarships/nl-scholarship-for-prospective-students.

How this was checked: Radboud Scholarship Programme and NL Scholarship pages on ru.nl read on 9 Nov 2026; the NLS page still carries some stale 2026 wording in its conditions list. Application fee not found.

01

What it pays

  • Tuition reduced to EUR 2,771 (amount to be confirmed), covering the nominal programme duration.
  • Covers costs for visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance.
  • EUR 5,000 NL Scholarship for one year, stackable with the RSP. You cannot get the NLS alone.
  • Living costs are not covered. You pay them from your own USD 30,000.

02

Who can apply

  • All non-EU/non-EEA nationals, which includes Bangladesh.
  • A bachelor's from outside the Netherlands and full admission to an English-taught master's.
  • Not for Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree masters. Two-year programmes require all first-year courses to be passed.

03

Dates that matter

  • 31 Jan 2027, 23:59 CET: submit in OSIRIS.
  • 14 Feb 2027, 23:59 CET: application complete, including two reference letters and a CV.
  • Before mid-April 2027: decision.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

  • This is a self-funded degree with a discount, so it spends your budget rather than saves it. A Dutch master's gives research skills and a European base, but it does not license you to practise in the Netherlands. A Sept 2027 start overlaps your internship and delays the 2029 Match.

05

The Dutch scheme context

  • Dutch universities fund international students through several partial awards. Radboud's RSP and NLS are capped at 22 each, Twente's UTS ranges EUR 3,000 to 22,000, and Maastricht's High Potential Scholarship pays EUR 1,550 a month to about 2% of applicants. Radboud is the cheapest in cash terms but does not fund living costs.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: partial only

    Rent and food come from your own money.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: amount to be confirmed

    The EUR 2,771 figure is flagged as 'to be confirmed' on the official page.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: quota

    At most 22 awards of each kind across all programmes.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: stale wording

    The NLS page's conditions list still shows 2026 dates in places, so confirm the 2027-28 terms.

07

The honest recommendation

  • Only worth a file if there is a Radboud master's you want and you accept the 2029 delay. Do not treat it as funding: it makes the degree cheaper, not free.

PortalUniversity of Twente Scholarship form ↗ (opens in a new tab)

You must be admitted to a Twente master's first, then complete the scholarship form (open 15 Oct 2026 09:00 CET to 1 Apr 2027 16:00 CET). An application fee was not confirmed on the page checked.

How this was checked: Scholarship page on utwente.nl read on 9 Nov 2026; amount, dates and eligibility confirmed there, fee not found.

01

What it pays

  • EUR 3,000 to 22,000 for one year.
  • A second year of the same amount is possible with an average of at least 7/10 and 50% of ECTS passed.
  • No costs are paid on your behalf: the award reduces what you pay, it does not cover fees, housing and living in one package.

02

Who can apply

  • Non-EU/EEA students. Bangladesh is on the eligible-countries list.
  • You must be admitted first to a Twente master's, and be in the top 5 to 10% of your class.
  • IELTS 6.5 (speaking 6.0). Not for ITC or pre-master programmes.

03

Dates that matter

  • 15 Oct 2026, 09:00 CET: scholarship form opened (September 2027 programmes).
  • 1 Apr 2027, 16:00 CET: form closes.
  • First week of May 2027: results.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

  • Same pattern as other Dutch master's: you spend your own money for a degree year that starts around Sept 2027, which overlaps your internship and delays the Match. It gives Europe-facing credentials without a licence.

05

The Dutch scheme context

  • Twente's award is one of several partial Dutch awards. Radboud's pair (EUR 2,771 tuition plus EUR 5,000) is smaller but more predictable; Maastricht's EUR 1,550 a month goes to about 2% of applicants. Twente's range is wide, so the real amount is the thing to ask about.

06

How this was identified

  • The Facebook reel from ApplyKite never named the scheme. It said only 'up to EUR 22,000, possible second year, deadline 1 April 2027'. Claude matched that amount and date to the official University of Twente Scholarship page and found them identical, so the identification is supported.

07

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: partial

    It can be as low as EUR 3,000.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: rank

    Top 5 to 10% needs a class-rank letter you do not yet have.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: admission first

    The scholarship is only for admitted students.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: wrong dates in the notes

    The notes' Twente deadlines of 1 Feb and 1 May do not match the official 1 Apr.

08

The honest recommendation

  • Only pursue it if a Twente master's fits your goals and you can show a top-decile ranking. Otherwise compare it with the funded Maastricht routes.

      01

      What it pays

      • PLN 2,500 a month, tuition exemption at public universities, and a PLN 2,500 travel allowance.

      02

      Who can apply

      • The 2026/27 call wanted a bachelor's no earlier than 2024 (or finished by 15 July 2026), no prior Master's, and B2 English.
      • Eligibility covers 36 listed countries; Bangladesh was reported eligible and not re-checked.

      03

      Dates that matter

      • Watch NAWA for the 2027/28 call.

      04

      How it fits the US and Europe goals

      A Polish Master's is a low-cost European base but not a licensing route.

        The call asks for a short self-presentation video.
